chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated from al-Abbas ibn Aamir, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurara ibn A'yun, from Abdul Malik ibn A'yun, who said:

I was with Abu Ja'far when the mention of al-Qa'im came up, so I said to him: 'I hope that his appearance is soon and that as-Sufyani does not precede it.' He said: 'By Allah, no! It is an inevitable matter that must occur.'

key_terms.السُّفْيَانِيُّ: as-Sufyani, a specific figure whose rise is a major sign of the end times
key_terms.الْقَائِمِ: al-Qa'im (The Riser), referring to the Twelfth Imam
key_terms.الْمُحْتَوَمِ: al-muhtawam, an inevitable or unavoidable matter

ai.seo_question: Will the rise of as-Sufyani occur before the appearance of al-Qa'im?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies the eschatological sequence by affirming that the rise of as-Sufyani is a divinely ordained necessity (*min al-mahmum*) rather than a contingent possibility. This establishes the Sufyani’s emergence as a pivotal precursor to the appearance of al-Qa'im, reinforcing the Shia belief in a structured cosmic timeline where major signs precede the Mahdi's advent.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (4) Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Sa’eed narrated from Ali bin al-Hasan from al-Abbas bin Aamir from Abdullah bin Bukayr from Zurara bin A’yun that Abdul Melik bin A’yun had said:

“Once I was with Abu Ja’far al-Baqir (as) when al-Qa’im (as) was mentioned before him. I said to him: “I hope that he (al-Qa’im) appears sooner without being preceded by the rising of as-Sufyani.” He said: “By Allah, that will not be! It is an inevitable thing.”
